question_text: A 29-year-old primigravid woman at 24 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a prenatal visit. She feels well. She has no personal history of serious illness. Medications include iron supplements and a multivitamin. Her temperature is 37.2°C (99°F) and blood pressure is 108/60 mm Hg. Pelvic examination shows a uterus consistent in size with a 24-week gestation. A 1-hour 50-g glucose challenge shows a glucose concentration of 155 mg/dL (N < 135 mg/dL). A 100-g oral glucose tolerance test shows glucose concentrations of 205 mg/dL (N < 180 mg/dL) and 154 mg/dL (N <140 mg/dL) at 1 and 3 hours, respectively. She refuses treatment with insulin. Which of the following complications is her infant at greatest risk of developing at birth?
